depiction.primary_object: rounded square outline containing an X mark

ambiguity: Strongly resembles a task status checkbox (canceled or skipped task) right next to the app's actual completion checkbox, or a window close button.

modifier_semantics.meaning: cancel, reject, close, or mark as not done

task_intents: abort or revoke a pending request

example_tasks.task: Cancel Planet Fitness membership in person before annual fee hits
Withdraw application for the senior product role at Stripe
Cancel the backordered sofa from West Elm and get deposit back
Revoke old OAuth app permissions on GitHub and Google accounts
Turn off auto-renewal on the New York Times digital access
Send the polite rejection email to the second roofing contractor
Check if we need 30 days notice
Clear out the remaining ones from Q3
Cancel the non-refundable hotel booking in Zurich and ask if they can waive the fee
Close the old joint checking account at Chase once the last utility auto-pay clears

example_tasks_es: Dar de baja el seguro del coche antiguo antes del viernes
Cancelar la suscripción de prueba de Apple TV+
Cerrar la cuenta bancaria de Santander que ya no usamos
example_tasks_ru: Отменить подписку на Яндекс Плюс до списания

context_tasks.task: Audit monthly recurring charges on the Amex statement
Draft sunsetting plan for the legacy v1 API
Review failed build logs from last night's deploy

near_misses.task: Fix the close button alignment on the modal dialog
Buy tic-tac-toe board for the coffee table
Download invoice for the cancelled flight to Berlin
Multiply the recipe quantities by 4 for Saturday's dinner
Vote in the municipal school board election on Tuesday

reasoning: A square box with an X inside is universally read as UI chrome (a window close button or a canceled/failed checkbox state in a to-do list). Placed beside a task in a task manager, it looks like the task's completion status rather than its subject, though it can weakly cue cancellation tasks.
